## `Predicate` · interface · [source](operations.aug#L3)

A pure decision about one data value. Supply an implementation, a matching standalone function, or a typed expression callback. The type parameters are `T` (accepts values) which must satisfy `optional Data`.

<a id="symbol-Predicate.accepts"></a>
### `Predicate.accepts` · [source](operations.aug#L4)

It takes `value` as `T`. It returns `bool`.

<a id="symbol-Transformation"></a>
## `Transformation` · interface · [source](operations.aug#L7)

A pure transformation of one data value into another. The type parameters are `T` (accepts values) which must satisfy `optional Data` and `U` (produces values) which must satisfy `optional Data`.

<a id="symbol-Transformation.apply"></a>
### `Transformation.apply` · [source](operations.aug#L8)

It takes `value` as `T`. It returns `U`.

<a id="symbol-Aggregator"></a>
## `Aggregator` · interface · [source](operations.aug#L11)

A pure aggregation step; the caller chooses the initial total. The type parameters are `T` (accepts values) which must satisfy `optional Data` and `U` which must satisfy `optional Data`.

<a id="symbol-Aggregator.combine"></a>
### `Aggregator.combine` · [source](operations.aug#L12)

It takes `total` as `U` and `value` as `T`. It returns `U`.

<a id="symbol-Comparator"></a>
## `Comparator` · interface · [source](operations.aug#L15)

A pure ordering: negative before, zero equal, positive after. Supply a consistent total order. The type parameters are `T` (accepts values) which must satisfy `optional Data`.

<a id="symbol-Comparator.compare"></a>
### `Comparator.compare` · [source](operations.aug#L16)

It takes `left` and `right` as `T`. It returns `int`.

<a id="symbol-filter"></a>
## `filter` · [source](operations.aug#L21)

Return a new list of matching values in snapshot order; an empty input returns an empty list.
Read references without copying their contents or granting mutable access.

It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `predicate` as [`Predicate<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate). It sets `selected` of type `List<T>` to a list with no items. For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, if [`predicate.accepts`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate.accepts) with `value` returns true, with temporary permission to change `selected`, it appends `value` to `selected`. After the loop, it returns `selected`. [source](operations.aug#L22-L27)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
filter<T>(List<T> values, Predicate<T> predicate) returns List<T>
```

The type parameters are `T` which must satisfy `optional Data`. It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `predicate` as [`Predicate<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate).

</details>

<a id="symbol-transform"></a>
## `transform` · [source](operations.aug#L32)

Transform every snapshot value once, preserving order in a new list.
An empty input returns an empty list. Transformations cannot mutate inputs or perform I/O.

It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `transformation` as [`Transformation<T,U>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Transformation).

It sets `transformed` of type `List<U>` to a list with no items. For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, it sets `result` to [`transformation.apply`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Transformation.apply) with `value`. With temporary permission to change `transformed`, it appends `result` to `transformed`. After the loop, it returns `transformed`. [source](operations.aug#L33-L38)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
transform<T, U>(List<T> values, Transformation<T,U> transformation) returns List<U>
```

The type parameters are `T` which must satisfy `optional Data` and `U` which must satisfy `optional Data`. It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `transformation` as [`Transformation<T,U>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Transformation).

</details>

<a id="symbol-aggregate"></a>
## `aggregate` · [source](operations.aug#L43)

Combine snapshot values from left to right, starting with initial.
An empty input returns initial. This operation does not choose a numeric overflow policy.

It takes `values` as `List<T>`, `aggregator` as [`Aggregator<T,U>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Aggregator), and `initial` as `U`. It sets `total` to `initial`. For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, it sets `total` to [`aggregator.combine`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Aggregator.combine) with `total` and `value`. After the loop, it returns `total`. [source](operations.aug#L44-L47)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
aggregate<T, U>(List<T> values, Aggregator<T,U> aggregator, U initial) returns U
```

The type parameters are `T` which must satisfy `optional Data` and `U` which must satisfy `optional Data`. It takes `values` as `List<T>`, `aggregator` as [`Aggregator<T,U>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Aggregator), and `initial` as `U`.

</details>

<a id="symbol-remove"></a>
## `remove` · [source](operations.aug#L50)

Return a new list without matching values, preserving snapshot order; do not mutate values. It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `predicate` as [`Predicate<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate).

It sets `remaining` of type `List<T>` to a list with no items. For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, if [`predicate.accepts`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate.accepts) with `value` returns false, with temporary permission to change `remaining`, it appends `value` to `remaining`. After the loop, it returns `remaining`. [source](operations.aug#L51-L56)

<a id="symbol-find"></a>
## `find` · [source](operations.aug#L61)

Read the first matching snapshot value or null, stopping after the first match.
A matching null value is also null; use an explicit loop when presence must be distinguished.

It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `predicate` as [`Predicate<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate). For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, if [`predicate.accepts`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate.accepts) with `value` returns true, it returns `value`. After the loop, it returns null. [source](operations.aug#L62-L65)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
find<T>(List<T> values, Predicate<T> predicate) returns optional T
```

The type parameters are `T` which must satisfy `optional Data`. It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `predicate` as [`Predicate<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Predicate).

</details>

<a id="symbol-sort"></a>
## `sort` · [source](operations.aug#L71)

Return a stably sorted copy. Equal values keep their input order; values remains unchanged.
Bottom-up merging uses O(n log n) comparisons and O(n) additional elements per merge pass; retained allocation depends on collection by the runtime.
Checked indexed reads retain IndexError in the contract; internal indices stay within the snapshot.

It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `comparator` as [`Comparator<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Comparator).

It sets `ordered` of type `List<T>` to a list with no items. For each `value` in a snapshot of `values`, with temporary permission to change `ordered`, it appends `value` to `ordered`. After the loop, it sets `length` to the number of elements in `ordered`. It sets `width` to `1`. [source](operations.aug#L72-L77)

While `width` is less than `length`, it sets `merged` of type `List<T>` to a list with no items. It sets `start` to `0`. While `start` is less than `length`, it sets `middle` to `length`. If `width` is less than (`length` minus `start`), it sets `middle` to `start` plus `width`. [source](operations.aug#L78-L116)

It sets `end` to `length`. If `width` is less than (`length` minus `middle`), it sets `end` to `middle` plus `width`. It sets `left` to `start`. It sets `right` to `middle`. [source](operations.aug#L85-L89)

While `left` is less than `middle` and `right` is less than `end`, it sets `earlier` to the item at index `left` in `ordered`. It sets `later` to the item at index `right` in `ordered`. If [`comparator.compare`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Comparator.compare) with `left` from `earlier` and `right` from `later` is at most `0`, with temporary permission to change `merged`, it appends `earlier` to `merged`. It increases `left` by `1`. [source](operations.aug#L90-L100)

Otherwise, with temporary permission to change `merged`, it appends `later` to `merged`. It increases `right` by `1`. After the loop, while `left` is less than `middle`, it sets `value` to the item at index `left` in `ordered`. With temporary permission to change `merged`, it appends `value` to `merged`. [source](operations.aug#L98-L105)

It increases `left` by `1`. After the loop, while `right` is less than `end`, it sets `value` to the item at index `right` in `ordered`. With temporary permission to change `merged`, it appends `value` to `merged`. It increases `right` by `1`. [source](operations.aug#L105-L110)

After the loop, it sets `start` to `end`. After the loop, it sets `ordered` to `merged`. If `width` is at least (`length` minus `width`), it sets `width` to `length`. Otherwise, it increases `width` by `width`. [source](operations.aug#L111-L116)

After the loop, it returns `ordered`. [source](operations.aug#L117)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
sort<T>(List<T> values, Comparator<T> comparator) returns List<T> unless IndexError
```

The type parameters are `T` which must satisfy `optional Data`. It takes `values` as `List<T>` and `comparator` as [`Comparator<T>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Comparator). Failures can raise `IndexError`.

</details>

<a id="symbol-IntegerOrder"></a>
## `IntegerOrder` · class · [source](operations.aug#L120)

Order integers without subtracting and overflowing at the int64 boundaries. It implements [`Comparator<int>`](operations.aug.md#symbol-Comparator).

<a id="symbol-IntegerOrder.compare"></a>
### `IntegerOrder.compare` · [source](operations.aug#L121)

It takes `left` and `right` as integers. If `left` is less than `right`, it returns `-1`. It returns `1` if `left` is greater than `right`, or `0` otherwise. [source](operations.aug#L122-L126)

<summary>Checked interface</summary>

</details>
